text: Shove is the most satisfying way to
handle your problems in Balders's Gate
3. However, it's likely the most
situational skill in the entire game.
With it, you need a high ground to deal
damage. You can't target the obese, and
sometimes it just fails for no apparent
reason. But what if you were a
massochist who enjoys restricting
yourself in stupid ways? Can you beat
Balders's Gate 3 using only Shove? The
rules for this run is everything with an
action cost is banned except for shove.
That remains true both in and out of
combat. So, no jumping to traverse
terrain, no lockpicking to open doors,
and no slurping up those delicious
potions unless they've been spilled out
on the ground via shove. The only
exception I'll be making is for equipped
items because Stone Cold said so. I
created a wood elf rogue for the extra
move speed, named myself Paul, assigned
the necessary hotkeys, and began my
pushy life. Shoving flying enemies such
as these imps has no effect, and without
a dash, the best you can do is briskly
walk away while using an attractive
female ally to distract. The second
tutorial encounter of the game nearly
took my life, even whilst on the easiest
difficulty. Clearly, Shadow Heart didn't
satisfy these imps in the same way. A
usual transponder takes us to Fyun, and
an atypical problem arises. Without
lockpick, stealth, or jumps being an
option, you need to fight the nearby
brain cats. A task which would likely be
impossible if not for this persistent
patch of fire in the wreckage. However,
even on Explorer, these brain cats are
no joke to these heroes. As planned, one
devourer burned. Not as planned, Shadow
Heart went down, and with one HP, Paul
the Pusher clutched victory. Short
resting is the only tool I currently
have to get Shadow Heart back up. And
from there, I pressed on to recruit some
muchneeded allies. Even with these two
burly bros at my side, we had no
feasible way to slay a 2HP mind flare on
the brink of death. Nor could I free
Lazelle, even if I wanted to, which I
don't. Upon reaching the Goblin Gate
speed bump, we shoved two different
goblins off this hill, somehow
impressing every resident of the grove
with our combat ability. Just once, I
wish these guys would have called me out
and questioned what the hell I was
doing. Within the grove, Will said he's
up for the challenge. And using assisted
parkour, the party was able to make its
way around back of this shack to get
into the crate supply room. More than
any run in the past, future proxy is
going to need these at some point down
the line. And upon reviewing this
script, past proxy did not know how much
of an understatement that really is.
Back in the wilderness, Scratch joined,
offering purely moral support. A small
stream broke my will as no amount of
trigonometry could locate the pixel
perfect shove position. Drought roleplay
may be illegal, but talking today is
not. That was actually the last video.
These cowardly village goblins gave up
instantly, unable to withstand my
yapping. Levers not being a shovable
entity means that Wilburn's a windmill
for life type of guy. Still don't know
why those cost an action, but doors
don't. Now at level three, I subclass
into a thief for that sweet second bonus
action. And after the handsome Gortach
cut scene, my party members followed
suit. Armed with eight total shelves per
each round of combat, we manhandled each
other over a bridge, unlocked the
waypoint, and pissed off the nearby
NLES, luring them to a ladder, and
repeatedly pushing them back down as
they climbed up worked brilliantly. This
challenge may not be as dumb as I
initially thought. Still nearly died,
but we came out on top over some of the
least intelligent creatures this world
has to offer. Attempts to take on the
range nles using a barrel wall for cover
did not quite go as well. Their ability
to block out your bonus actions forced
the first of what will be many
gameovers. Paladins of Tear nearly
caused the second, but thanks to my best
friend, Mr. Ladder, we had a chance.
Sometimes getting up after you've been
knocked down is not such great advice.
Did make a bit of a mistake here,
though, as having no short rest after
the fight meant I had no way to get my
party back up off the dance floor. And I
discovered just how nightmarish trying
to kill your own allies in this run.
Really is. The least painful method I
could find involved shoving an alchemist
fire to burn them alive. And 600 gold
later, Withers fixed that mistake.
Counselor Floric lucked out that God's
gift to crate engineering was nearby.
Her life is saved despite not deserving
it. Dialoguing to level four unlocked
our first feat. And after a close
examination of all her options, I
settled on the most boring one, ability
score to strength. If there's one bit of
feedback I could give for Larry's next
game is, please make the feats more
interesting than this list of crap. For
a bit more loot, I open these lock
chests the same way the caveman used to
do it, dropping them off a bridge to
crack them open. The goblin camp being
filled with chasms means it's one of the
few locations in this world my party
isn't complete garbage, especially with
the amount of pushing my party packs.
This works excellently against enemies
already close to a chasm. But after a
bit of thought, I'd come up with a very
slightly better method. Back in the
Grove, Alfra was met, and she taught me
how to play a musical instrument.
Performing in Boulders's Gate 3 has no
action cost, and it lures your enemies
to where you're standing. It doesn't
always work, but when it does, the
enemies are in prime pushing position.
Menthara fell for the ruse, as did many
others. Before wrapping up the goblin
camp, I took on the challenge of
reaching the swamp island. Again,
teamwork got us there, and the note was
obtained. With it, we were able to
expose Kaga. And as it's a battle you
can win by doing absolutely nothing, I
was not about to miss out on that free
XP. More importantly though is with that
wrapped up, you can claim the idol
without starting a war. The druids
aren't stupid enough to let you just
pick it up, but they are stupid enough
to not be bothered by someone shoving it
over and over. Okay, they're a little
bothered, but you can just shove your
allies out of any criminal accusation to
get off scot-free. Eventually, I got it
over to the beach where the only witness
here was a bear. And what the hell is he
going to do? The best ring I'll ever see
was given to me by this child. I
returned to the goblin camp to sacrifice
a dozen more foes to the river goddess.
Ogres, much like your mother, are far
too heavy for me to deal with. So, the
party helped each other move along until
reaching the door for our escape. Side
note, while continuing to lure the
goblins, I learned that playing an
instrument poorly can trigger them to
throw a rock at you. A pretty cool
interaction that I'd never seen before.
Going into this, I knew the goblin camp
would be the most fun of this
playthrough. Draw Raglin and his crew
fell into these bottomless pits. A
makeshift staircase got me all the
explosives from the camp, and with them,
it was off to solve a second grade under
darkdark circle puzzle. Gail is
volunttored to be the mushroom face tank
and miraculously he didn't trigger any
of them as he ran through this
minefield. Impressive to say the least.
Nearby, I picked up a nearby saucer
flower as it's entirely a buff and took
the first boat over to Grim Forge to
continue my fun. The battles here did
get tougher, but because act one is a
masterpiece in level design, there were
plenty of tools at my disposal. At
times, this meme eight shves per turn
build was feeling a little broken. Far
according to the forge waypoint was
simpler than I'd ever imagined it would
be. Just two shves is all she took. And
if you weren't aware, this sussy flower
aura disables these animated armors,
making a free win and even freer win.
While you can't use shove to mine for
ore, you can use shove from a makeshift
tower to get the job done. From here,
reaching the forge is not a problem, but
pulling the lever using shove is an
obstacle I could not overcome.
Explosives don't trigger it. You can't
shove it. And honestly, I'm fine with
taking an L. To feel better, I hosted a
pool party with the local Dwagar, and
all were invited. Before wrapping up the
location, there was one more item, I
better say set of items that my party
would like to take from Grim Forge. The
golden masks. They may not have any
description on their tool tip as to what
they do. But if you wear these masks,
they increase the strength score of
nearby allies by one. I had two already,
and for the last two, I just had to
bypass this locked door. I was able to
engineer this solution to get me over
the cage into the first room. These pain
in the ass signs were methodically
shoved off a cliff, and another tower
constructed to get to the second floor
mass storage area. The final door is
opened using a key, and now all you have
to do is somehow defeat all of these
enemies without using a chasm.
Repositioning the enemies down to Gale
was the plan, and I'd hoped that they
would repeatedly climb the tower to face
a certain doom. It looked promising at
first until they absolutely obliterated
my build. As Paul had the high ground, I
bombarded the enemy from above using
whatever trash I'd picked up along the
way here, ultimately finishing them with
a smoke powder satchel. With all four of
these masks, the entire party is now
rocking 21 strength. Pretty nice, as
long as you don't look at their other
stats. Overall, things have gone much
better than I expected throughout act
one. But as we enter the mountain pass,
I don't have high hopes. I used the
attack option to instigate a battle with
these outdoor gith as it's one
confrontation I felt about 81% confident
in engaging in combat in areas you
normally just don't bother with rather
enjoyable even if the AI gets a little
janky because of it. The cools being one
of the most cost effective time to XP
ratio fights in the game meant I was not
going to skip it. A rooftop should have
made it easy but because shove requires
pixel perfect accuracy to do anything,
it was not. I would have been furious if
not for this cobalt inventor murking
literally every single one of his allies
with an alchemist fire. To thank him, he
was given a hasty death. The Gishkas,
too, were supposed to be a free win. But
for some unexplainable reason, these
hairless abominations cannot be shoved
off a cliff. Much like a flying
creature, when shoved into the Grand
Canyon, they reappear unharmed where
they once were. Embarrassingly, I was
game over by several hairless cat freaks
due to a mechanic literally no one knows
about. Regular viewers of this channel
know I love exterminating the gith as
much as the next guy. But after
searching around the monastery, I
couldn't really think of an easy way to
do it. With low ceilings, a lack of
elevation, and no recreational chasms,
it's a shoveproof fortress. I had to
apologize to Shadow Heart, as very
little Gith racism will be had in this
story. The undead block in the road were
led on a wild goose chase and dealt with
accordingly. I do appreciate that Larry
gave so many creatures in this game
ladder climbing animations, even though
you normally don't see them. I might
actually handle the undead this way in
my future runs, too, because Chasms
handled that self-revive problem quite
well. Now, in act two, I asked politely
for the DRE to give me his lantern,
pixie, shopped around last light in, and
entered moonrise. Chasms may be
plentiful here, but the thought of
luring the enemies over to them for the
next 3 to 4 hours was a nightmare I just
wasn't willing to experience. The prison
basement, though, has some of the most
easily accessible pits in the game. So,
I started here and waited as the magical
floaty eyeballs called down my victims.
I bet you this is what it feels like to
be the alliance in AV. Hunger of Hadar
was annoying, but not in a worldending
kind of way. To stay alive, I shoved
healing potions down from my makeshift
towers until victory was assured.
Metagaming the rest of Moonrise on the
easiest difficulty sounds pretty lame.
So instead, I headed straight through
the curse into the most fun section, the
Gauntlet of Char, another area with a
lot of verticality. Just so long as you
lure them over to the corner of death,
they'll die without much difficulty.
It's in the name after all. The gigantic
Umbreal portal room has no chasms, but
using my extensive lack of respect for
my own time, I was able to kite them all
back to the death corner. Rocking 24 AC
as a level five rogue with the uncanny
evasion passive means pretty much
nothing's going to kill me. The whole
process took two trips and roughly 2
hours. At one point, I got so bored of
waiting for my enemy turns, I began
examining potatoes and other random food
items in my inventory. I hoped to find a
secret in these texts to Larry's future
games. However, my priorities being
elsewhere was nearly my undoing. Charge
warriors were downing my allies. Before
I even knew what was happening, I was
alone. I splashed a potion on the floor
to lick it up and hid behind my barrel
wall. Annoyingly, several of these
undead survived being shoved off a
cliff, leading to a 49 round battle
before I could clean it all up. With
that near disaster avoided were ready to
face Lady Char's trials. The softstep
trial I figured to be pretty simple.
Turn-based mode to walk by the ghosts,
build a tower, and push someone over the
gate. Didn't work though. Don't know
why. So, I had to get someone else to go
get me the key by shoving them through
this small gap in the wall. Overall,
it's about a four out of 10 on the pain
in my ass scale. The cell same trial, I
sent Gail in naked to hopefully cheese
the fight with a weaker clone. I
expected this fight to be a joke, what
with that chasm being right there. But
what me of the past was unaware of is
that these copies are completely
unshoveable. My first attempt to lure it
onto a box over the chasm and shove the
box out from under its feet completely
failed. The next strategy involved
gathering several cobalt in a barrel and
surprise shoving them in the direction
of my clone. Aiming with shove is a
mystery not even the world's greatest
scientist could comprehend. That plan
failed. I tried to lure them over with
Will and for a third time, my plan was
unsuccessful. As a naked, unarmed copy
of Will easily kicked four cobalt asses.
Plan four, bombing from above. As
previously established, aiming near
impossible, but at least against a melee
combatant, you can lure them into a
pre-established bombard zone, bringing
an end to a 9 out of 10 on the pain in
my ass scale. As I cleaned up after
myself, I wonder what the hell I'm doing
with my life. A sentence I'm sure many
of my viewers have said in the past,
just not in this context. Momentarily,
the faith leap child path appeared
visible. Still wish I knew why the hell
it does that sometimes. And despite the
shove only restriction having no bearing
on one's ability to complete it. I still
died twice while walking through the
maze. Two out of 10. Jurgger's gem is
next. Two dozen one HP rats next to a
chasm were obviously no contest for this
party. But what threw me for a loop was
at the end of the fight that Justicier
dude never spawned. I was worried the
quest was now broken and I ran around
confused for much too long until just
going to check in with Jurgger.
Apparently, I'd already completed the
quest without even knowing it. Guessing
that just spawned into the chasm earlier
and instantly died before I met him.
Regardless, that's all four gems. Not
time to deal with the night song,
though, long way before that. Shadow Art
needs her spear or she's going to whine
and complain. Char's librarians joined
their brethren in the pit, which took
much longer than usual due to this
individual phasing through reality and
being stuck under the map. I've got a
strange feeling that no one else tested
shove to these extremes. After braving
the bugs, I got my spear, my umbil gems
are placed, the shadow fell unlocked,
and now Belely. It might seem obvious
that fighting Beltazar in the Shadowfell
makes the most sense. What with that
zone being basically a gigantic chasm,
but you'll see why shortly. I think that
would be a disaster. Instead, Bely gave
chase out of the bedroom while his
undead followers were barricaded behind
chests. He too joined the pit party,
diving in like a poorly trained Olympic
swimmer. Only one more task to complete
before starting the Shadowfell,
purchasing bombs off of quartermaster
tally, then spamming long rest to
refresher items and doing it over again.
Canonically, we spent 6 months doing
this, stockpiling more bombs than the
Canadian military, which isn't really
saying much. For me, this took 52
minutes, but for you, just a few
seconds. Just like clicking that
subscribe button, you lazy. Finally, the
time you've all been waiting for. The
first of the game's impossible jumping
puzzles. Going into this, I was fairly
confident that this obstacle was going
to kill the run. Like, how the hell does
one cross eight platforms using only
shove? So, here's how. The first space
rock is in range of the second for an
easy start. A single crate can be placed
and picked up without an action to drop
yourself to the third. To prevent your
characters from auto jumping like
uncontrolled monkeys, their items must
be packed with 1,000 kg of garbage as
they're abandoned. If you're too heavy,
you can't jump. The fourth space rock is
bypassed by a shove directly to the
fifth. And from there, one person can be
shoved down to the sixth mineral.
However, once you reach this location,
you're stuck. And whenever I'm stuck,
proxy box science commences. The only
thing I could really think of was to
find a way to detonate an ottoloid tank
and propel myself off this ledge. But
because the terrain here is so jank, all
the usual methods I had just wouldn't
work. No matter my positioning, I
couldn't find a way to shove an
alchemist fire into this location using
just two characters. I tried using a
tower with shadow heart from the low
ground, but that [ __ ] aiming on shove
made it quite impossible. The
experiments continued until I had an
idea. Wine barrel. I could shove this
off of a box tower to create an alcohol
surface, equip a torch, and ignite it.
Boom goes the tank. Down goes the will.
Afterwards, a final big box tower is
constructed until I find the magical
blue line leading to the night song. At
this rate, I may as well change my name
to Boxy Gate Tactician, as they do end
up solving most of my problems. Getting
Shadow Heart to this point is crucial,
as to avoid using the help action later
on in the game, she must spear the night
song. This may not be a shove, but it's
also not an action. I really love this
game. Happy, proud, and feeling rather
accomplished, I left behind the
impossible jumping puzzle. The remaining
party members were too far away to reach
the exit portal, so the pixie port
technique was used to escape the red
zones. The safety railings at Moonrise
were rather frustrating to deal with.
But because some sections are broken,
enemies could be lured over and shoved
off. One by one, these cultists were
passed along like batons in a race to
their death. All except for the
necromancer chick. Just ignored her to
walk on by for the confrontation with
Katherine. As many of you are aware,
Katherine is unshoveable because screw
you. There's also not much high ground
up here to make use of. So once again,
proxy boxy tactics come into play. From
five crates high, a shoved smoke powder
bomb will detonate on impact to deal
damage. The easier way for you cheesers
at home is to just stack 20 bombs at his
feet and one-shot Kather. But that felt
a little bit outside the spirit of the
challenge. The strategy worked well and
to my surprise, Katherrick even managed
to topple a couple of them. But in the
end, his loss was inevitable. Within the
colony, a small membrane was not enough
to block our path. Nice try, villains.
And further in, I freed us as I believe
it's the only summon in the game which
doesn't take any action or bonus actions
to call to your side. Any nearby
valuables were of course gathered. We
elevated down. And before battle, I
constructed a few crate towers using the
item fling glitch to position them
around the room. But for roleplay, let's
pretend that was magic. The usual
problem of aim being impossible remains.
And in this room, it's worse than ever.
Not sure if it's due to all the random
breaks in terrain the room has going on,
but my explosives nearly always fall
directly down, smashing the towers I
built. Very frustrating to say the
least. Mid battle, Kather styled on us
like a pro gamer. He downed Gail and in
the same turn threw a healing potion to
get him back up. I don't need your
sympathy, bro. Most of the time, it's a
solid strategy in this encounter to
clear out Kather's allies before he
transitions. But with my crap DPS, it
was not happening. Instead, we turned
our attention purely on the boss.
Repeatedly obliterating my own crates
was not a problem I forsaw going into
this. And due to that scenario, a
problem never before seen in the history
of proxy challenge runs occurred. My box
supply was completely tapped. I anyways
played it out to the end. Fantasy Gi
timing, though things looked bleak. As
the towers disappeared, unknowingly, one
of my crates still had a box in prime
shoving position, waiting until my next
turn. And Kather the bozo cleaved it,
taking his own life. Didn't even realize
that was a possibility. So, thanks,
Kather. That's one Nether Stone down,
and with it, it's off to meet some
Yanks. A practice run of my path was
trial. By this point, I'd learned I can
equip and unequip Crusher's ring to get
an extra 3 m of move speed per turn.
Doesn't sound like much, but it did help
immensely in getting to the portal in
just two rounds. Again, in space, our
second jumping puzzle begins. The first
fight is handled with ease using a
couple of shves. And once again, time is
going to be spent to discover this
golden angle in order to reach a further
space rock. Two towers and 37 minutes
later, it was found. I'd originally
thought that turning into a frog to
reduce my weight would increase the
shoving range of my characters. But
despite the tool tip saying that shove
range is affected by your weight, that's
a complete lie. And being 1 kg changes
absolutely nothing. Tool tippers, get it
together. Continuous tower shoving
enabled our hero Paul to be the lone
soldier on this final space rock. At
least us was at our side. Alone, I'd say
this fight is a level 10 on the pain in
my ass scale. Finding that pixel perfect
pushing path is about as hard as it is
to say that sentence. And if they get a
whole person on you, then take your
hands off the keyboard, buddy. You're
dead. I gave it a few tries and decided
the best tactic is to run away. Towards
the back of this asteroid, there's less
random crap to block your paths. And if
they're busy hitting the emperor, it
gives you extra time you need to win.
The god run occurred when the emperor
was soloing the gith, and I save him
through all the stuns. Shocking, right?
It's pretty safe to say that on a higher
difficulty, this fight would have broken
me into the city we went, successfully
shoving our way through two ax. The
guard checkpoint obstacle was bypassed
thanks to our iron hand brethren. Then
to get into the keep, I plan to parkour
around the side and use this door here.
But unlike other entities in this game,
this door appears to be bombproof. I
don't know why that is, so screw me for
trying to be creative. I'm just going to
talk my way into the keep. Within the
castle, I attended the coronation of
Gortach himself and invited him to play
a game of past the handsome young man,
shoving him towards the balcony in just
one round of combat. I bited my time for
a couple of rounds until all of his bus
fell off and then Humpty Dumpti the
tyrant. Looked pretty fun, so I Humpty
Dumptied myself off too, surviving due
to the rogue fall damage resistance
passive, which was absolutely planned
and not an accident. That's a lie. My
assassination was complete and an escape
was made. My one regret was that I
didn't grab the waypoint before doing
so. To nobody's surprise, boxes are
again the solution. An invis potion
cracked upon the floor was necessary to
survive a casual walk through the keep.
And once you arrive in the lower city,
the brain finally clears you of your
crimes. Anyone who's followed one of the
many god-awful build guides on the
internet knows that this is the region
where your build will finally come
online. Even dog [ __ ] sh ones like this.
I brought a out of retirement to speak
with Kazador's guards, getting us a key
to the mansion. And in here, we stole
the chest from the basement, cracking it
open like an oyster to reveal the pearl
that is the helm of grit, the best in
slot shovel helm. When below 50% HP, it
grants you an additional bonus action.
Three shves per turn is achieved. Now,
to track down Orin, we need to commit a
few murders. The only target even
somewhat viable is Nesa down by the sea.
Like a psychopath, I proceeded to push
her and any other nearby innocent
witnesses down the stairs, several
times, in fact. And after that wasn't
really killing people with the speed I'd
hoped for, I settled on drowning them in
the ocean. Thanks to Gortach already
being dead, any of the steel watchers in
the city are already neutral, as they're
under the brains control. Any regular
humanoid citizen or guard can easily be
handled with a bit of shoving. I say
easily, but I didn't say fast. Archers
constantly hugging walls is brutal for
my team. Our ballist bro, Olf Faith
Olm's daughter, hung out to watch the
whole thing go down from start to
finish, putting me on the trail of a
murderer named Dolar. A re-release of a
20-year-old game temporarily paused the
challenge. Todd Howard got me to buy
horse armor again. And upon returning to
Balders's Gate, I shoved the murderer's
gang, then ran to the guards like a
coward. They stopped that criminal scum
right there. Off this murderer's corpse,
the tombstone password is obtained. But
unfortunately, there's no key. On the
plus side, that door proved particularly
vulnerable to fire. Funny enough, this
fight has never been a challenge to me
in the past, but trying to kill a
chained up elephant using only shove
proved much more difficult than one
might imagine. The elephant itself is
unshoveable. If you try to use an
explosive, it breaks the chains, causing
any nearby spectators to turn against
you. Alchemist fire, though, that's
cool. Even though I accidentally hit
Sarave, he brushed it off like it was
nothing. That elephant barbecue brings
us to level 9, and Serave hands over the
amulet of ball, tasking us to go kill
his daughter. family goals into the
sewers, through the door, and walk
through Manslaughter Chasm to get up to
the Ball Temple. This is one fight I was
dreading more than any other. Up until
now, I've been looting barrels all game
long, and honestly had no idea why. So,
I decided, let's just randomly plop them
all over the place and see what happens.
Barrels often break the AI in this game.
Attempt number one was going pretty
well. The channelers were dealt with
over time, and I'd brought more than
enough crates after that near disaster
incident with Kather. A long 35-minute
fight ensued until suddenly I was moving
a crate, and this happened.
While funny and weird, it was rather
annoying. Attempt number two, and my
defenses were absolutely decimated. Orin
was also rather painful to deal with as
she would continuously topple any towers
I construct. What's even worse is during
this attempt, I noticed that she can ou
any damage my pathetic party is capable
of putting out. With that game over
being nowhere near close, I decided that
a brute force method probably isn't the
best option. It's time to engage my
brain. I broke open a barrel of brine to
lay down a costic surface and had my
whole party stand in it to drop our
health below 50%. Which took a
surprisingly long time on explore. Next,
I broke open four separate invisibility
potions on the floor, slurped them up,
and sent in the gang to shove Orin
towards the edge of the chasm. Once you
